sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submit that the petitioners had granted a franchise for Rajnandgaon to a partnership firm operating as Fashion Interior Institute of India for the period 5 May 2017 to 4 May 2020.
Respondent No. 2, Mukesh Sahu, was only associated with the franchisee as a representative and had no independent contractual or financial dealings with the petitioners.
After the franchise ended, the petitioners continued to provide academic support to enrolled students subject to payment of dues.
Mukesh Sahu later attempted to obtain the franchise but failed to meet the required criteria.

Subsequently, in 2021, he started an institution under a deceptively similar name, allegedly misrepresenting himself as affiliated with the petitioners, leading to legal notices, trademark proceedings, and an order from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs directing him to change the company name.

It has been further submitted that the complainant alleged that six students were not allotted marksheets by the present petitioners, whereas, out of those six students, two students have already cleared their dues to the university and received the marksheets also and other four students were informed by petitioners on several occasions regarding payment of their outstanding dues and thereafter collection of marksheets, but they failed to respond to such communications and collect the marksheets after clearing their respective dues.
The petitioners contend that the criminal proceedings initiated against them are baseless and arise out of a purely civil dispute.
No elements of cheating or criminal breach of trust are made out, as there was no inducement, entrustment, or contractual relationship with Mukesh Sahu.

It is settled law that if a mater is fundamentally a civil dispute, such as a breach of contract or a property dispute, then initiating criminal proceedings for it, is an abuse of the legal process and present dispute, if any, is purely of a civil dispute category.
Therefore, the criminal proceedings against the petitioners may be stayed.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioners, purely as an interim measure it is ordered that the further proceeding of Criminal Case No.11306/2025 pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate Rajnandgaon, (C.G.) arising out of the FIR No.388/2025 registered by Kotwali Police Station, Rajnandgaon (C.G.) for the offence under Sections 405, 420, 120(b) r/w 34 of the IPC and Final Report 544/2025, shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
Issue notice to respondent No.2 on payment of P.F. as per rules.

List this case after service of notice upon respondent No.2.
 Sd/- Sd/-
 (Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) (Ramesh Sinha)
